message.content:
### Tenant Rights in Texas (as of 2024) | Area | Key Rights & Protections | |------|--------------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within **30 days** after the lease ends, minus any lawful deductions (e.g., damage beyond normal wear). | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must keep the property in a safe, livable condition—plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity, pest control, etc.
• If the landlord fails to maintain habitability, tenants can withhold rent, repair and deduct, or terminate the lease. | | **Lease Terms** | • Written lease is required for leases longer than one year.
• Landlord cannot impose unreasonable restrictions; any clause that violates Texas law (e.g., discrimination, illegal activity) is void. | | **Rent Increases** | • For month‑to‑month leases, landlords must give **30 days’ written notice** before raising rent.
• For fixed‑term leases, rent can only increase at the start of a new term unless otherwise specified. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must provide a **30‑day notice** for nonpayment of rent or a **60‑day notice** for lease termination without cause.
• Eviction requires a court order; landlords cannot forcibly remove tenants. | | **Discrimination** | • Protected classes under Texas law: race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, age, marital status, and source of income. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Tenants have the right to live without unreasonable interference from the landlord or other tenants. | | **Repair and Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to fix major problems, tenants may repair the issue and deduct the cost from rent, provided they follow proper procedures (e.g., giving notice, obtaining receipts). | | **Notice of Entry** | • Landlord must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hours) before entering the unit, except in emergencies. | | **Lease Termination** | • Tenants can terminate a lease early if the landlord breaches habitability or other lease terms, but must follow the lease’s termination clause or provide proper notice. | | **Legal Remedies** | • Tenants can file a claim in small claims court for unpaid security deposits or damages. | | **Resources** | • Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA) – tenant‑landlord handbook.
• Texas Attorney General’s Office – consumer protection section.
• Local tenant advocacy groups (e.g., Texas Tenants Union). | #### Quick Tips for Tenants 1. **Read Your Lease Carefully** – Understand all clauses, especially those about rent, deposits, repairs, and termination. 2. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of all communications, receipts, and photos of the unit. 3. **Know Your Notice Periods** – Whether you’re paying rent or moving out, know how much notice you need to give the landlord. 4. **Report Problems Promptly** – Notify the landlord in writing about any maintenance issues. 5. **Seek Legal Advice if Needed** – If you believe your rights are being violated, consult a tenant‑rights attorney or local advocacy group. --- **Disclaimer:** This information is general in nature and not legal advice. Laws can change, and specific circumstances may affect your rights. For personalized guidance, consider contacting a licensed attorney or a local tenant‑rights organization.
